## The centred linear polynomials (`type: cp3`, `cp5`) {#sec-ch04-cp}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0 (chengcli/snapy)
sources: OUTLINE.md chapter 4, scheme 4.5

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- Fixed-weight linear face interpolants of third and fifth order, with no limiter.
- Switches: `type: cp3`, `type: cp5`; they are also the `interp2` partners of `weno3` and `weno5`.
- Reach their nominal order on a smooth field and oscillate across a discontinuity.
- The even-width helpers `cp2`, `cp4`, `cp6` exist for the upwind-biased forms and are not selectable.
:::

These are the plain polynomial reconstructions: fit a polynomial through a fixed number of neighbouring cell
averages and evaluate it at the face. Nothing adapts, so they are the fast and accurate choice where the field
is smooth and the wrong choice across a shock. They matter beyond their own switch because they are what the
velocity and pressure rows actually use whenever a deck selects a WENO type (@sec-ch04-framework).

### Derivation

The weights are determined by requiring the formula to be exact when the underlying field is a polynomial of
degree up to one less than the stencil width, with the cells carrying *averages* rather than point values.
`[C1]` checks this symbolically rather than by assertion: for each of `cp2`, `cp3`, `cp4`, `cp5` and `cp6` it
raises the degree of a test polynomial until the formula first fails, and recovers exactly the nominal order in
every case, that is exact through degree one, two, three, four and five respectively.

Because the cells carry averages, the weights are *not* the Lagrange weights for point values; the distinction
is the same one that section 4B is built on, and getting it wrong is the easiest way to lose an order.

`[C4]` then measures the face error on a smooth monotone profile and finds fitted orders of 3.02 for `cp3` and
5.02 for `cp5` over $n_1 = 16 \to 64$. The same measurement through two critical points leaves `cp3` at 2.99:
a linear scheme does not care about critical points, which is exactly the contrast @sec-ch04-weno needs.

### Numerical method

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch04-cp-order
#| fig-cap: "Measured face error of the four selectable high-order interpolants against resolution. (a) On a monotone profile with no critical point in the domain, each reaches its design order: the two linear polynomials (blue circles, sky-blue squares) and the two WENO forms (vermillion triangles, green diamonds) lie on top of one another. (b) Through two critical points the linear cp3 keeps order three while weno3 falls to order two; the dotted lines are reference slopes. Data from the committed output of the chapter's reconstruction check."
#| fig-alt: "Two log-log panels of maximum face error against cell count, each with four series, and reference slope lines in the right panel."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch04.fig_recon_order import make_fig
make_fig()
```

The weights are written out as rationals at `interp_cp3` ([`interp_simple.hpp:73-75`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interp_simple.hpp#L73-L75)) for `cp3` and
`interp_cp5` ([`interp_simple.hpp:110-114`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interp_simple.hpp#L110-L114)) for `cp5`; `cp2`, `cp4` and `cp6` sit beside them at
`interp_cp2` ([`interp_simple.hpp:43-45`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interp_simple.hpp#L43-L45)), `interp_cp4` ([`interp_simple.hpp:79-82`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interp_simple.hpp#L79-L82)) and
`interp_cp6` ([`interp_simple.hpp:118-121`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/recon/interp_simple.hpp#L118-L121)). The even-width three are not registered as types: they exist because
the upwind-biased forms `bp2`, `bp3` and `bp5` are built from them as a centred part plus a dissipative part.
Those upwind forms are themselves unreachable at this pin, with no type string selecting them.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- No limiter. Across a discontinuity these interpolants oscillate, and nothing in the scheme detects that; the
  floors of @sec-ch04-framework are the only thing standing between an overshoot and a negative density.
:::

1. **Uniform weights.** The rationals assume equal cell widths, so the measured orders above are orders on a
   uniform grid only.
2. **Unreachable code.** The even-width polynomials and all three upwind-biased forms are compiled and never
   called at this pin.
